title: Batch 14 verify leftovers
description:
- [JMAP-skk9.6] minor crate-jmap-tasks-types/PLAN.md: Doc drift at lines 295-296: the field table still lists TaskFilterCondition after/before as wire type `UTCDate`. After this commit and under draft-ietf-jmap-calendars-33 §5.11.1 the wire type is LocalDateTime. This is a planning doc, not rustdoc or the README, so it is not blocking. (crate-jmap-calendars-types/PLAN.md:328-329 says `String|null — LocalDateTime`, which is still accurate as a wire description.)
- [JMAP-skk9.7] minor crate-jmap-tasks-types/src/task.rs: The example in the Task struct doc (line 244) is wrong. `serde_json::from_value::<Location>(task.locations.clone().unwrap())` decodes the whole id->Location map as one Location, when each entry should be decoded separately. The same mistake was there before this commit, but this commit changed these exact fields and left the example in place. The CHANGELOG entry gets it right ('Decode entries with serde_json::from_value'). The doc example should do the same, e.g. iterate over `.as_object()` values.
- [JMAP-skk9.7] minor crate-jmap-tasks-types/src/task_list.rs: Outside the bead's scope (the bead names only Task/CalendarEvent fields), but it is the same kind of sibling divergence. TaskList.default_alerts_with_time / default_alerts_without_time (lines 180, 185) are Option<BTreeMap<Id, Value>>, while calendars Calendar (calendar.rs:151, 155) uses Option<BTreeMap<String, Value>>. Changing either later is also a semver break. Not blocking for JMAP-skk9.7. It could be filed as its own bead if wanted.
- [JMAP-skk9.8] minor crate-jmap-chat-client/src/calendars.rs: The commit message says the compile_fail doctests pin rejection with E0004, but both doctests (calendars.rs:24 and crate-jmap-filenode-client/src/methods/filenode.rs:69) use a bare `compile_fail`, not `compile_fail,E0004`. They would still pass if the snippet failed for some unrelated reason. The risk is low because the snippets are trivial, but the commit message overstates what is checked. Changing them to `compile_fail,E0004` would make the claim true (rustdoc checks error codes only on nightly).
- [JMAP-skk9.8] minor crate-jmap-filenode-client/README.md: Pre-existing and out of scope for this bead: the FileNodeOnExists table at README.md:120-128 lists only Replace and Rename, missing Newest and Unchanged (added under JMAP-4vf8.19). It also does not mention the new #[non_exhaustive]. This commit did not introduce the drift, but it is the only user-facing doc for this enum. A follow-up bead would track it.
- [JMAP-skk9.9] minor crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/calendar.rs: The commit loosens the all-None guard in calendar_set, participant_identity_set (crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/participant_identity.rs) and address_book_set (crate-jmap-contacts-client/src/methods/addressbook.rs) to `&& !sets_default`, but no test covers the reject side. Nothing asserts that all-None with params None, or with Some(params) where on_success_set_is_default is None and only extra or on_destroy_* is set, still returns ClientError::InvalidArgument without sending a request. grep finds no InvalidArgument assertion for any of these setters in either crate's tests. The guard had no negative test before this commit either, but the condition is new code. Suggested fix: add one negative test per setter.
- [JMAP-skk9.11] minor crate-jmap-chat-mimi-client/README.md: Doc drift: the server README's Gotchas now says openmls is a re-exported public dependency and that a new openmls minor means a major release. The client README's Dependencies section (line ~61) still lists only `openmls =0.9.1`; it does not mention `jmap_chat_mimi_client::openmls` or the major-bump policy. lib.rs, AGENTS.md and CHANGELOG do cover it, so this is minor.
- [JMAP-wf92.25] minor crate-jmap-mail-server/src/mailbox.rs: No negative test for the CHANGELOG-announced behaviour change: a Mailbox comparator with a non-boolean isAscending (or another malformed field) now gets invalidArguments instead of being read as ascending (mailbox_sort_arg, line ~159). The only unknown-property test (integration.rs:14298) covers Mailbox/queryChanges, not Mailbox/query.
- [JMAP-wf92.25] minor CHANGELOG.md: The generic handle_query/handle_query_changes for EmailSubmission, ShareNotification, FileNode and CalendarEventNotification now reject malformed comparators (e.g. sort:[5]) with invalidArguments, where O::Comparator = Value used to accept any JSON. This is correct per RFC 8620 §5.5, but the CHANGELOG lists this only for Mailbox. A conforming peer would not observe it.
- [JMAP-wf92.26] minor crate-jmap-types/src/lib.rs: Out of scope for this change and not a defect in it. jmap-types (lib.rs:33 `pub mod backend` plus lib.rs:51 `pub use backend::{GetObject, JmapObject, QueryObject, SetObject}`) and jmap-server (lib.rs:35/39) still give their items two public paths. JMAP-wf92.26 names only the seven *-types crates, and all seven are done. If the one-public-path rule is meant to cover the whole workspace, these two crates need a decision in a separate bead.
- [JMAP-wf92.24] minor crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/event.rs: The doc comment on copy_non_public_event_into_foreign_account_is_invalid_properties says 'A public copy into the same account still succeeds', but the last assertion copies from 'own' into the foreign 'shared' account. It is not the same account. The comment should say something like 'A public copy into the foreign account still succeeds'. The test logic is correct.
- [JMAP-wf92.27] minor crate-jmap-server/src/lib.rs: The commit body says it addresses JMAP-wf92.20, but nothing in the diff touches it and there is no follow-up bead for it. The core jmap-server crate still exposes both `pub mod handlers` and `pub mod backend` and re-exports their items at the crate root. JMAP-wf92.26 covers only the types crates and JMAP-26di.47 covers only jmap-chat-client; `bd search` for 'pub mod handlers', 'dual-path' and 're-export' finds nothing for jmap-server. The finding itself asked for a follow-up bead, so one should be filed, or the commit body should stop claiming .20 is addressed.
- [JMAP-wf92.27] minor crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/memory.rs: The new module doc (lines 22-25) says both the §5.9 privacy_conflicts hook and the §5.10 may_copy_calendar_event hook fail open 'since this backend has no account-ownership model'. That reason fits only §5.10. The §5.9 uid/privacy check needs no ownership model: it could be computed from the events MemoryBackend already stores, as the cfg(test) MockBackend does. The doc gives a wrong reason for leaving §5.9 unimplemented.
close_reason: batch 14b: committed, adversarially verified, CI green at 1ed6fa86
